title: Find the first or last occurrence of a given number in a sorted array
problemStatement: Find the first and last index of a target in a sorted array with duplicates.
intuition: Do not stop at the first match — keep searching the side that could contain an earlier (or later) occurrence.

approaches.title: Optimal: two boundary binary searches
approaches.dryRun:
a=[5,7,7,8,8,10] target=8
lower_bound -> 3
upper_bound -> 5, so last = 4 -> (3,4)
approaches.whyWorks: Equal values occupy a contiguous block in a sorted array.

edgeCases: All elements equal to the target
commonMistakes: Returning on the first match instead of continuing the search
Forgetting to validate that a[first] actually equals the target
patternRecognition: Frequency / range queries on sorted data -> two boundary searches
followUps: Extend to counting in a range [lo, hi]
interviewInsight: Deriving last = upper_bound - 1 rather than writing a second bespoke loop is the clean answer.

related.title: Count occurrences of a number in a sorted array with duplicates
